A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 23-page paper, including Appendices A–E. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that only the first-page arXiv version/date stamp changes; the research content is fully comparable.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, ablations, and qualitative results in Section 5, plus human studies and a DanceGRPO transfer experiment in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark results, ablations, human studies, and transfer experiment in Section 5 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: The two-stage directional correction and generator alignment procedure, reward objectives, and components are identical in Section 4.2 and Appendix A, including Algorithms 1–2.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same HPDv2, GenEval, and DivGenBench coverage, including identity, style, layout, and tonal diversity. No training or evaluation domain or scenario changes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout: FLUX, DanceGRPO, Flow-GRPO, and SRPO in the main comparisons, the same ablation variants, and the same DanceGRPO transfer comparison in Appendix D.3.

E3.justification: The FLUX.1.Dev backbone, reward configurations, metrics, training budgets, and evaluation procedures remain identical. Appendix D retains the same human-study sample sizes and designs.

E4.justification: Figure 7 retains the same vector-convergence, guidance-scale, and learned-vector ablations. The DanceGRPO generalizability experiment in Appendix D.3 and qualitative analyses in Appendix E are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 3 retains random seed 42, and Appendix D retains the same seed-control information. Repeated-run information, uncertainty reporting, and statistical-testing practices do not change.

E6.justification: All numerical results, plotted trends, and qualitative examples are identical, including Tables 1–2 and 6–7. The reported overall HPDv2 user preference for D2-Align remains 48.2% in Figure 8.

T1.justification: The diffusion and reward equations, algorithmic mathematics, and definitions of IDS, ASC, SDI, and PVS in Appendix C are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims concerning Preference Mode Collapse, DivGenBench, and D2-Align's ability to improve preference alignment while preserving diversity.

C2.justification: The explanations attributing collapse to reward-model biases and interpreting directional correction as preserving diversity remain identical. No limitations, applicability boundaries, or interpretations of the empirical results change.

D1.justification: Appendix B and Table 3 retain identical hardware, optimizer, hyperparameter, training, and inference details. Code/data access and other reproducibility information are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the positioning against earlier alignment and diversity research, and all 69 references are unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv margin header changes from v1 dated 30 Dec 2025 to v2 dated 10 Mar 2026. The title, authors, prose, terminology, and document structure are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: Figures, tables, captions, and page layout remain identical, including all appendix visualizations. Rendered pages 2–23 match exactly; the sole first-page difference is the version/date stamp covered under P1.

improvement.justification: The only visible revision is the arXiv version/date stamp. The scientific content, empirical evidence, explanations, reproducibility details, and appendix material are identical, establishing no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
